existing_mapping.evidence: The system includes functions for managing parking lots and storing related details.
The administrator is shown as an actor responsible for updating parking lot details.
The system handles the information about the number of available spaces in parking lots.
The gate sensor actor detects vehicle arrivals and departures, communicating this to the system.
Upon vehicle arrival, the system verifies vehicle details using data from the gate sensor.
If vehicle verification is successful, the system opens the gate barrier.
There are instructions for clients to access the system if the barrier does not open automatically.
Clients are required to enter personal information and provide vehicle photos for system access.
The system uses uploaded photos to extract detailed vehicle information.
The system categorizes vehicle colors into predefined groups during the extraction process.
The system updates associations between vehicles and clients in the database to ensure correct pairing.
Once updates are complete, the system instructs the opening of the gate barrier.
Parking session details are stored after the vehicle passes the barrier.
Clients follow procedure to leave their vehicle in the parking, involved with conveyor operations.
The Conveyors’ Controller carries out scanning, conveyor assignment and runs optimization algorithms.
Parking spaces and conveyors have their locations represented by floor number and (x, y) coordinates.
Parking spaces are categorized by size to determine accommodation capacity.
Each conveyor has a specified maximum vehicle weight it can transport.
The optimization algorithm uses parking space size and conveyor weight capacity considerations.
System updates occur after moving vehicle to designated space with final location noted.
The system maintains awareness of vehicle locations, whether on conveyors or in parking spaces.
SMS notifications are sent to clients with details of their parking.
Parking details are accessible through the system UI with phone number entry.
Conveyor data is not retained post-parking session unless needed for problem resolution.
Clients retrieve their vehicles by using the system UI to enter their vehicle and phone numbers.
Conveyors are used to transport vehicles to the gate when ending a parking session.
The system UI prompts for client payment at the end of the parking session.
Payment calculations are based on IRS-provided price lists in JSON format.
Different parking lots may apply varying price lists including different pricing structures.
Price history for each parking lot is maintained by the system.
An external Payment Gateway manages the financial transaction processing.
The system waits for payment approval from the gateway before instructing the gate to open.
Receipts can be issued to clients per request including transaction specifics.
Receipts detail client and vehicle information, hours, pricing rate, and total amount.
A client club is managed by ParkWise to offer member advantages.
Parking discounts are automatically applied for club members.
Club registration is facilitated through the system user interface.
Club membership is described as a lifetime offer without cost.
Clients can choose preferred lots with storage dates preserved for records.
The first parking session for club members is free during registration month at chosen lots.
Administrators have the capability to generate various company reports.
Annual reports cover income and club member details comprehensively.
Annual reports feature financial statistics and parking colors.
Reports are sorted by city in descending order and by amounts in ascending order.
Output formats for reports include PDF and XML.
Monthly overviews showcase club member growth.
Club growth reports provide monthly member statistics and growth percentage.
Reports are organized by ascending month for year-long analysis.
